rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that he gave only a small amount, or gave only a little.
rows.anchor: أي شيئا قليلا أو إعطاءا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akdā means he stopped short, from digging until a hard layer of earth prevents further digging.
rows.anchor: أي قطع من قولهم حفر فأكدي إذا بلغ إلى كدية

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: They identify al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: after nearly accepting Islam, he was dissuaded by a polytheist who promised to bear his afterlife burden for payment; al-Walid paid some, then withheld the rest.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وابن زيد : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة كان قد سمع قراءة رسول الله

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse concerns al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who paid five to a poor emigrant to make him apostatize and promised to bear his sin.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : هو النضر بن الحرث أعطى خمس لفقير من المهاجرين حتى ارتد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the referent as al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, who agreed with the Prophet on some matters.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي كان يوافق النبي

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says it concerns Abu Jahl, who remarked that Muhammad commands only noble character traits.
rows.anchor: وقال محمدبن كعب : في أبي جهل قال : والله يأمر محمد إلا بمكارم الأخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls the al-Walid account the best-known and most fitting because the next verse asks whether he has knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: والأول هو الأشهر الأنسب لما بعده من قوله سبحانه : ( أعنده علم الغيب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري في الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf's story that Uthman gave a camel to Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh, then stopped charity after being promised release from his sins, is false and baseless; Uthman is above this.
rows.anchor: وأما ما في الكشاف من أنها نزلت في عثمان بن عفان رضي الله تعالى عنه كان يعطي ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here afara'ayta means tell me; its first object is the relative pronoun and its second is the following interrogative clause.
rows.anchor: و ( أفرأيت ) هنا على ما في البحر بمعنى أخبرني ومفعولها الأول الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa introduces a consequence of the preceding question: does he possess unseen knowledge, and therefore know his companion will bear his burden at Judgment?
rows.anchor: والفاء في قوله تعالى : ( فهو يرى ( للتسبب عما قبله أي أعنده علم بالأمور الغيبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible sense is that he sees what he heard from the Qur'an as false.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يرى أن ما سمعه من القرآن باطل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi takes the question to mean: was a Qur'an sent down to him, so that he judged his conduct right?
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : المعنى أأنزل عليه قرآن فرأى أن ما صنعه حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb most readily describes inward perception, though it may also mean physical sight of what is hidden from others.
rows.anchor: وأيا ما كان فيرى من الرؤية القلبية وجوز أن تكون من الرؤية البصرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am lam yunabba here means rather, has he not been informed?
rows.anchor: ( أم لم ينبأ ( أي بل ألم يخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scrolls of Moses are the Torah.
rows.anchor: ( بما في صحف موسى ( وهي التوراة

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explains that a person is not rewarded for another's deed, following the statement that he is not held accountable for another's sin.
rows.anchor: بيان لعدم إثابة الإنسان بعمل غيره إثر بيان عدم مؤاخذته بذنب غيره

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-anna is coordinated like the preceding wa-anna; mā may be a verbal noun, or a relative pronoun meaning only what he strove to do.
rows.anchor: كأختها السابقة و ( ما ) مصدرية وجوز كونها موصولة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A man asked the Prophet whether his deceased mother would be rewarded if he gave charity for her, since she died suddenly without speaking; the Prophet answered yes.
rows.anchor: ما أخرجه مسلم والبخاري وأبو داود والنسائي عن عائشة أن رجلا قال لرسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A man told the Prophet his sister had vowed to perform pilgrimage but died; the Prophet compared it to paying her debt and said God's debt is more deserving of payment.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : أتى رجل النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فقال : إن أختي نذرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reply is that when another intends an act for someone, that person is like the principal represented by an agent, so the act counts as his by proxy; this relies on figurative usage or combining literal and figurative senses.
rows.anchor: بأن الغير لما نوى ذلك الفعل له صار بمنزلة الوكيل عنه القائم مقامه شرعأ فكأنه بسعيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reply is that another's act benefits him only when built on his own effort of faith, so it can be treated as his effort.
rows.anchor: بأن سعي غيره لما لم ينفعه إلا مبنيا على سعي نفسه من الأيمان فكأنه سعيه

rows.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده
rows.claim: A report says al-As ibn Wa'il had vowed one hundred camels before Islam; Hisham sacrificed fifty, and Amr asked the Prophet, who said his father's fasting and charity would benefit him if he had affirmed monotheism.
rows.anchor: ما أخرجه أحمد عن عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده أن العاص بن وائل نذر في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same reply is offered to the objection that verses promising multiplied reward conflict with the restriction to one's own effort.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم ما في الجواب من النظر

rows.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: Husayn ibn al-Fadl answered Ibn Tahir that by justice a person has only what he strove for, while by grace God may grant whatever He wills; Ibn Tahir approved him.
rows.anchor: ليس لهبالعدل إلا ما سعى وله بالفضل ما شاء الله تعالى فقبل عبد الله رأس الحسين

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says this rule applied to the teachings of Abraham and Moses, whereas people of this community may benefit from another's effort.
rows.anchor: عكرمة : كان هذاالحكمفي قول إبراهيم وموسى

rows.speaker: سعد بن عبادة
rows.claim: Sa'd ibn Ubada asked whether his mother would benefit from voluntary charity given for her, and the Prophet said yes.
rows.anchor: يدل عليه حديث سعد بن عبادة هل لأمي إذا تطوعت عنها قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : نعم

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabi takes al-insān, the human, here to mean the unbeliever; a believer receives both his own effort and what others do for him.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع : الأنسان هنا الكافر وأما المؤمن فله ما سعى وما سعى له غيره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to say the verse was abrogated by the promise that believing descendants would be joined to their believing ancestors in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن الآية منسوخة بقوله تعالى : ( والذين آمنوا واتبعتهم ذرياتهم بإيمان

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the abrogation report as unsound: this is a report, not a command, and reports are not abrogated.
rows.anchor: أبو حيان رواية النسخ بأنها لا تصح لأن الآية خبر لم تتضمن تكليفاولا نسخ في الأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative to abrogation is that the report described earlier scriptures and was later specified for this community; that is a qualification of the report, not abrogation.
rows.anchor: تقييد الأخبار لا إلى النسخ إذ حقيقته أن يراد المعنى ثم من بعدذلك ترتفع إرادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the lām as ʿalā, meaning against a person, is far from the apparent wording and the context admonishing one who turned away and gave little.
rows.anchor: وقيلأ : اللام بمعنى على أي ليس على الإنسان غير سعيه وهو بعيد

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya's preferred clarification is that a person can truly claim only his own effort; intercession, a righteous relative, or multiplied reward belongs to him only figuratively or by attribution.
rows.anchor: والتحرير عندي في هذه الآية أن ملاك المعنى هو اللام من قوله سبحانه : ( للإنسان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this clarification, the verse does not prove the Mu'tazilite claim that gifting any reward to another is void, or the Shafi'i argument that recitation's reward cannot reach the dead.
rows.anchor: استدلال المعتزلة بالآية على أن العبد إذاجعل ثواب عمله أي عمل كان لغيره

rows.speaker: ابن الهمام
rows.claim: Ibn al-Humam says Malik and al-Shafi'i distinguish bodily worship from other acts: they deny transfer of pure bodily worship such as prayer and recitation, but accept acts such as charity and pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام ابن الهمام : إن مالكا والشافعيلا يقولان بوصول العبادات البدنية المحضة

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi says the well-known Shafi'i position and that of a group is that recitation's reward does not reach the dead; Ahmad and a group of scholars, including some Shafi'is, hold that it does.
rows.anchor: المشهور من مذهب الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه وجماعة أنها لا تصل وذهب أحمد بن حنبل وجماعة من العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author recommends asking God after recitation to convey its reward to the deceased; he says this suffices outwardly, though some require intention at the beginning.
rows.anchor: فالأختيار أن يقول القاريء بعدفراغه اللهمأوصل ثواب ما قرأنه إلى فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the reward apparently does not reach the dead when the Qur'an is recited for payment, since the paid recitation earns no reward; payment for teaching is not prohibited.
rows.anchor: أما غذا كانت بها كما يفعله أكثر الناس اليوم فإنهم يعطون حفظة القرآن أجرة

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji says the actual dispute concerns whether another person can perform bodily worship as a proxy and discharge the obligated person's duty, with or without permission and during or after life.
rows.anchor: الخفاجي : هو محتاج إلى التحرير وتحريره أن محل الخلاف العبادة البدنية هل تقبل النيابة

rows.speaker: الطحاوي
rows.claim: Al-Tahawi says the report that a deceased person’s heir fasts on their behalf belongs to early Islam and was later abrogated; the proxy rule is established for pilgrimage, not fasting.
rows.anchor: فقالأ الطحاوي : إنه كان في صدر الإسلام ثم نسخ

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: The dispute is not about substitute payments such as feeding, or gifting reward: the latter is a supplication whose acceptance comes through God's grace, like charity for another.
rows.anchor: ليس الكلام في الفدية وإطعام الطعام فإنهبدل وكذا إهداء الثواب سواء كان بعينه أو مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His effort will be shown and disclosed to him on Judgment Day in his record and scale.
rows.anchor: يعرض عليه ويكشف له يومالقيامة في صحيفته وميزانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form is from araytuhu al-shayʾ, I showed him the thing; the display brings glad tidings to the good-doer and rebuke to the evil-doer.
rows.anchor: من أريته الشيء وفي البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creatures end and return to God alone at the Resurrection; no other has an independent or shared role in that final return.
rows.anchor: أي إن انتهاء الخلق ورجوعهم إليه تعالى لا إلى غيره سبحانه استقلالا ولا اشتراكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several commentators gloss the destination as God's reckoning, reward in Paradise, or punishment in the Fire.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال غير واحد : أي إلى حساب ربك أو إلى ثوابه تعالى من الجنة وعقابه من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes God the limit of thought: inquiry into realities stops when it reaches the divine essence and attributes.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى أنه عز وجل منتهى الأفكار فلا تزال الأغكار تسير

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: A report from Ubayy ibn Ka'b attributes to the Prophet the statement that there is no thinking about the Lord.
rows.anchor: وأيد بما أخرجه البغوي عن أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه قال في الآية : لا فكرة في الرب

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Abu al-Shaykh transmits from Sufyan al-Thawri a Prophetic report: when the Lord is mentioned, stop there.
rows.anchor: وأخرجه أبو الشيخ في العظمة عن سفيان الثوري وروي عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام إذا ذكر الرب فانتهوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet told people contemplating God to contemplate creation instead, since they could not encompass the Creator.
rows.anchor: ابن ماجة عن ابن عباس قال : مر النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم على قوم يتفكرون في الله

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet saying to contemplate God's creation and not God, lest one perish.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر قالأ : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : تفكروا في خلق الله ولا تفكروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the passage supports those who hold that God's essence cannot be known in its full reality; he notes that most transmitted proofs point this way.
rows.anchor: أكثر الأدلة النقلية على عدم الوقوع

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads inna with kasra here and in the following instances, treating these clauses as disconnected from what precedes and not among the scrolls' contents.
rows.anchor: أبو السمال وإن بالكسر هنا وفيما بعدعلى أن الجمل منقطعة عما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqna means that God bestowed possessions that remain and endure, such as gardens, livestock, and buildings; these precious assets merit separate mention despite being included in enrichment.
rows.anchor: وأعطى القنية وهو ما يبقى ويدوم من الأموال ببقاء نفسه أو أصله كالرياض والحيوان والبناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, qaniya al-māl means he acquired wealth; the verb also occurs with the hamza or doubled consonant, as aqnāhu or qannāhu.
rows.anchor: قنيت المال أي كسبته ويعدى أيضابالهمزة والتضعيف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses aghnā as making someone wealthy and aqnā as making him content.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ( أغنى ) مول ( وأقنى ) أرضى

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib explains contentment as a figurative form of possession: God gives a reserve of contentment and obedience, the greatest of treasures.
rows.anchor: الراغب : وتحقيق ذلك أنه جعل له قنية منالرضا والطاعة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد والأخفش
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and al-Akhfash understand aqnā as impoverishing, treating the hamza as privative, as in ashkā.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن زيد والأخفش ( اقتنى ) أفقر ووجه بأنهما جعلا الهمزة فيه للسلب والإزالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A different explanation of impoverishing takes aqnā as giving contentment and patience as one's lasting possession, preserving the pairing of opposites like causing death and life or laughter and tears.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنهما جعلا ( أقنى ) بمعنى جعل له الرضا والصبر قنية كناية عن ذلك ليظهر فيه الطباق

rows.speaker: الحضرمي
rows.claim: Al-Hadrami says God enriched Himself and made creatures poor before Him; al-Ālūsī objects that applying the implicit object this way sounds awkward and risks a wrong implication, and says the object is omitted because the acts themselves are the focus.
rows.anchor: وفسره بأفقر أيضا الحضرمي إلا أنه كما أخرج عنه ابن جرير وأبو الشيخ قال ( أغنى ) نفسه سبحانه و ( أفقر ) الخلائق إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon split apart into two portions during the Prophet's time in Mecca, about five years before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: انفصل بعضه عن بعض وصار فرقتين وذلك على عهد رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قبل الهجرة بنحو خمس سنين

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: In a sound report from Anas, the Meccans asked the Prophet for a sign and he showed them the moon split in two, with Mount Hira visible between its halves.
rows.anchor: فقد صح من رواية الشيخين وابن جرير عن أنس أن أهل مكة سألوه عليه الصلاة والسلام أن يريه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: In reports in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, Ibn Mas'ud says one half of the moon was over the mountain and the other below it; the Prophet told people to bear witness.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيحين وغيرهما من حديث ابن مسعود انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فرقتين

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Another Ibn Mas'ud report says Quraysh called it magic and proposed asking travelers; travelers who arrived confirmed seeing the split, after which the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: ومن حديثه أيضا انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام فقالت قريش : هذا سحر ابن أبي كبشة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A weak report from Ibn Abbas says a group of named Meccan opponents demanded a two-part split, promised to believe, and saw the halves over Abu Qubays and Qaynuqa on the night of Badr.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو نعيم في الدلائل عن ابن عباس من وجه ضعيف قال : اجتمع المشركون على عهد رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars disagree over whether the moon-splitting reports are mass-transmitted; the Sharḥ al-Mawāqif says they are, and al-Subki selects that judgment because the Qur'an states it and sound reports come by many routes.
rows.anchor: واختلف في تواتره فقيل : هو غيرمتواتر وفي شرح المواقف الشريفي أنه متواتر الذي اختاره العلامة ابن السبكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound versions come from several Companions, including Ali, Anas, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Hudhayfa, Jubayr ibn Mut'im, and Ibn Umar; some were too young or absent to witness it, which does not invalidate the reports.
rows.anchor: وقد جاءت أحاديثه في روايات صحيحة عن جماعة من الصحابة منهم علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وأنس وابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report locating the event at Mina does not conflict with Anas's report locating it at Mecca: the Prophet was then living in Mecca before the Hijra, and the Mina report does not say he was there.
rows.anchor: ولا يعارض ما صح عن أنس أن ذلك بمكة لأنه لم يصرح بأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان ليتئذ بمكة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report through Mujahid and Abu Ma'mar says Ibn Mas'ud saw the moon split into two portions twice in Mecca before the Prophet's departure.
rows.anchor: من طريق مجاهد عن أبي معمر عن ابن مسعود قال : رأيت القمر منشقا شقتين مرتين بمكة

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar says the claimed consensus may concern the splitting, not its happening twice, since he knows no hadith scholar who affirmed two separate events; he suggests twice might mean two halves.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ ابن حجر : أظن أن قوله : بالإجماع يتعلق بانشق لا بمرتين فإني لا أعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says twice modifies Ibn Mas'ud's seeing, not the splitting: he looked away and looked again, seeing the same split, which confirms the vision without multiplying events.
rows.anchor: والذي عندي في تأويل ذلك أن مرتين في كلام ابن مسعود قيد للرؤية وتعددها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through Ata from Ibn Abbas describes Meccans rubbing their eyes and looking again before calling the split moon magic.
rows.anchor: أخرج أبو نعيم من طريق عطاء عن ابن عباس قال : انتهى أهل مكة إلى النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says a report of seeing the split several times can describe repeated looking rather than repeated splitting; those who looked away and looked again still saw the same event.
rows.anchor: فلوقال أحدهؤلاء رأيت القمرمنشقا ثلاث مرات على معنى الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of the Ibn Abbas report describes Meccans rubbing their eyes, looking again, and still seeing the moon split before calling it magic.
rows.anchor: قالوا بأبصارهم فمسحوها ثم أعادوا النظر

rows.speaker: البوصيري
rows.claim: Al-Busiri's line about the Prophet's chest being split and the moon split for him is cited as support for a full-moon night, since the full moon is on the fourteenth.
rows.anchor: البوصيري في قوله : شق عن صدره وشق له البلد

rows.speaker: ابن حجر الهيتمي
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami takes the wording al-badr rather than al-qamar to suggest the fourteenth night; al-Ālūsī knows no precedent for this and allows that al-badr means the moon generally.
rows.anchor: ما في قول العلامة ابن حجر الهيتي في شرحه : الظاهر التعبير بالبدر دون القمر أن الشق كان ليلة أربع عشرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the moon was eclipsed during the Prophet's time, people called it bewitched, and the passage from this verse through 'mustamir' was revealed; eclipses most often fall on the fourteenth.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد كونه ليلة البدر ما أخرجه الطبراني وابن مردويه من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال : كسف القمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no need to read that eclipse report as a synonym for splitting: an eclipse could have occurred together with the splitting.
rows.anchor: ولا ضرورة إلى حمل الكسوف في هذا الخبر على الانشقاق إذ لا مانع كما في البداية والنهاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two portions remained in the sky, separated briefly, and then joined; the story that the moon entered the Prophet's sleeve and came out of his garment is baseless.
rows.anchor: ثم إن القمر بعد انشقاقه لم تفارق قطعته السماء بل بقيتا فيها متباعدتين تباعدا ما لحظة ثم اتصلتا

rows.speaker: بدر الدين الزركشي عن شيخه العماد بن كثير
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi relates from his teacher Ibn Kathir that the sleeve story is fabricated and has no basis; the author condemns its fabricator.
rows.anchor: باطل لا أصل له كما حكاه الشيخ بدر الدين الزركشي عن شيخه العماد بن كثير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The report through al-Dahhak that two moons appeared over Safa and Marwa until night is unreliable; it conflicts with sound reports by making Jews, rather than Meccan opponents, request the sign and say it was magic.
rows.anchor: وما في خبر أبي نعيم الذي أخرجه من طريق الضحاك عن ابن عباس من أنه انشق فصار قمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The popular claim that the Prophet pointed at the moon with his index finger is not found in a sound report.
rows.anchor: وقد شاع أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أشارإلى القمر بسبابته الشريفة

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Philosophers deny the splitting because they claim rupture and reunion are impossible for celestial bodies; al-Ālūsī calls their proof flimsy and says scholars of truth have refuted it.
rows.anchor: وأنكر الفلاسفة أصل الانشقاق بناءا على زعمهماستحالة الخرق والالتئام على الأجرام العلوية

rows.speaker: بعض الملاحدة
rows.claim: An objector argues that a cosmic event should have been universally observed and transmitted, yet reports are concentrated among Meccans, old histories and astronomical records omit it, and the event is physically implausible.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الملاحدة : لو وقعلنقل متواترا واشترك أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that the split occurred briefly at night, when people were inattentive, and different lunar risings mean the moon was not visible everywhere at once; astronomy was also less developed.
rows.anchor: والجواب عن ذلك أنه وقع في الليل وزمان الغفلة وكان في زمان قليل ورؤية القمر في بلد لا تستلزم رؤيته

rows.speaker: بعض الملاحدة
rows.claim: The objector further says rupture of so huge a body should make a sound vastly stronger than thunder and kill much of Earth's population.
rows.anchor: وأيضا لا يعقل لخرق هذا الجرم العظيم وأيضا خرقه يوجب صوتا هائلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī denies that a vast sound or harm must follow and notes that unusual events can occur without known causes; the speed of sunlight illustrates that motion can be extraordinarily rapid.
rows.anchor: ومثله ذهاب التجاذب والجسام مختلفة من حيث الخواص

rows.speaker: بعض الملاحدة
rows.claim: The objector argues that once split, the moon's pieces would lose mutual attraction and remain separated for years, as a divided mountain would.
rows.anchor: وأيضا متى خرق وصار قطعتينذهبت منه قوة التجاذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says celestial bodies need not share Earth's properties and offers that a separated portion could remain within Earth's gravitational reach; the physical objections do not establish impossibility.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون إحدى القطعتين كالجبل العظيم بالنسبة إلى الأرض إذا ارتفع عنها بقاسر مثلا جذبته إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By way of argument, he points to unfamiliar visual phenomena, the eye's unexplained operation, and reports of the evil eye to show that people can reject effects whose causes they do not understand.
rows.anchor: على سبب الإبصار بالعين على الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparisons are dialectical concessions; ultimately God's will suffices for this miracle, and requiring a cause for every event would entail an infinite regress.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله من باب المماشاة وإلا فإراة الله تعالى كافية في الأنشقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once possibility and God's encompassing power are established, these physical replies are unnecessary; God does what He wills.
rows.anchor: شمول قدرته عز وجل وأنه سبحانه فعال لما يريد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the splitting will occur after the second trumpet blast; the past tense expresses certainty of the future event.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أنه قال : هذا الانشقاق بعد النفخة الثانية والتعبير بالماضي لتحقق الوقوع

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: The same future interpretation is also reported from Ata.
rows.anchor: وروي ذلك عن عطاء أيضا ويؤيد الذي عليه الأكثرون قراءة حذيفة

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: The majority's view that the event occurred before the Resurrection is supported by Hudhayfa's reading, qad inshaqqa al-qamar, 'the moon has split.'
rows.anchor: ويؤيد الذي عليه الأكثرون قراءة حذيفة وقد انشق القمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī follows the majority: Hudhayfa's wording is a circumstantial clause indicating that the split happened as the Hour drew near, before the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: فإن الجملة عليها حالية فتقتضي المقارنة لاقتراب الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī concludes that deniers provide only improbability, not evidence of intrinsic impossibility.
rows.anchor: والحاصلأنه ليس عند المنكر سوى الأستبعاد ولا يستطيع أن يأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the blessing of teaching the Qur'an, the sūra next mentions creating humanity because humanity is the recipient of blessings.
rows.anchor: ثم أتبع سبحانه نعمة تعليم القرآن بخلق الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation for the order is that Qur'anic teaching is the greatest blessing; another is that human creation points to the goal of human perfection in knowledge, which precedes its subject mentally though not in external reality.
rows.anchor: لأنه أعظمها وقيل : لأنه مشير إلى الغاية من خلق الإنسان وهو كماله في قوة العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān means humanity as a species; creating it means bringing it into being with its outward and inward faculties.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالإنسان الجنس وبخلقه إنشاؤه على ما هو عليه من القوى الظاهرة والباطنة
